newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela CANTV shareholders OK stock listing.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela CANTV shareholders OK stock listing.

text.p: Shareholders of Venezuelan telephone company CANTV approved Monday the registering of shares with the National Securities Commission (CNV) in preparation for a forthcoming global issue of 40 percent of the company's stock, the company said in a release.

Shareholders also approved a modification in company statutes to allow suspend sales of the 11 percent of class C shares held by workers until 180 days after the global issue of the government's remaining stake in CANTV scheduled for late November.

Organized sales of C shares will subsequently be held every six months. Retired workers and heirs may sell up to 50 percent of their stock at each sale. Active workers with over 1,000 shares will be able to sell up to 20 percent while those with under 1,000 can sell up to 30 percent.
CANTV was partially privatized in 1991 when the VenWorld consortium led by GTE Corp bought a 40 percent stake. Workers bought another 11 percent of the company.

Of the remaining government stake, nine percent has been earmarked for workers. These class B shares will automatically become class C shares after they are acquired by workers, the CANTV release said.

The VenWorld consortium is led by GTE Corp with a 51 percent stake. Local utility Electricidad de Caracas holds 16 percent, Telefonica de Espana 16 percent, local bank Banco Mercantil 12 percent, and AT&T five percent.
